features.basis: KRAS-mutant lines (KPNSI9S, SNU410, GSU_STOMACH) are among the most killed, consistent with MAPK-pathway dependency
BRAF-mutant melanomas (LOXIMVI, UACC62, K029AX) and HEC265 are selectively killed, suggesting MAPK-driven sensitivity
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and appears in multiple sensitive lines (KALS1, LOXIMVI, BICR6, S117_THYROID)
EGFR-mutant NSCLC lines (NCIH1650, HCC4006, KYSE270) are among the most killed, indicating RTK-driven dependency
PTEN loss co-activates PI3K/AKT and is enriched in sensitive lines (KALS1, UACC62, HEC265, ZR751)
PIK3CA mutations appear in several sensitive lines (HGC27, KYSE510), suggesting PI3K-pathway addiction
MET mutation in HGC27, a highly sensitive gastric line, suggests RTK-driven sensitivity
KIT mutation in KYSE510, a sensitive esophageal line, suggests RTK dependency
NF2 loss in SNU410 and S117_THYROID, both sensitive, may deregulate Hippo/PI3K signaling
STK11 loss in KALS1, a sensitive glioma line, may impair metabolic stress responses
NRAS-mutant lines (KU1919, IPC298) are among the least affected, suggesting NRAS alone does not confer sensitivity
TP53 mutations are common in both sensitive and resistant lines, so they are not sufficient for selectivity

raw.explanation: Zolantidine is annotated as a histamine H2 receptor antagonist, but the selective killing pattern is not explained by H2 receptor biology; instead, sensitivity tracks with RAS/RTK-MAPK pathway activation (KRAS, BRAF, NF1, EGFR, MET, KIT mutations) and with loss of tumor suppressors that co-activate PI3K/AKT signaling (PTEN, PIK3CA, NF2, STK11). The most plausible mechanism is that zolantidine, like its transcriptionally similar reference drugs (estrogen receptor antagonist clomifene, TGF-beta receptor inhibitor D-4476, serotonin receptor antagonist R-96544, dopamine receptor antagonist flupentixol), has off-target activity that preferentially kills cells dependent on MAPK/PI3K signaling, while lines with intact or alternative survival signaling (e.g., NRAS-only, PIK3CA-only, or wild-type RAS/RAF) are protected. This would predict sensitivity in additional RAS/RAF/RTK-driven lines and resistance in lines lacking these dependencies.
